note.text:
The perpendicular bisector of [AB] is the line that cuts [AB] at its midpoint and makes a right angle (90°) with it. 'Perpendicular' means 'at a right angle'; 'bisector' means 'it cuts into two equal parts'.

Property: every point on the perpendicular bisector of [AB] is at the same distance from A and from B. If P is on it, then PA = PB.
Converse: if PA = PB, then P is on the perpendicular bisector of [AB].

To construct it with a ruler and compasses:
1. Open the compasses to more than half of AB.
2. Put the point on A and draw an arc above and below [AB].
3. With the same opening, put the point on B and draw arcs that cut the first two.
4. Join the two crossing points with your ruler.
The line you draw cuts [AB] at its midpoint.

worked_example.problem: AB = {d} cm. Choose a compass opening to construct the perpendicular bisector of [AB], and find where it cuts [AB].
steps: The opening must be more than half of AB: {d} ÷ {two} = {d / two} cm.
{r} cm is more than {d / two} cm, so an opening of {r} cm works.
With the point on A and then on B, draw arcs of radius {r} cm above and below [AB]. Join the two crossing points.
Each crossing point C is {r} cm from A and {r} cm from B: CA = CB, so C is on the perpendicular bisector.
The line cuts [AB] at its midpoint I, with AI = IB = {d / two} cm.
worked_example.answer: Use an opening of {r} cm. The perpendicular bisector cuts [AB] at I, with AI = IB = {d / two} cm.

wrong.text: If PA = {x} cm and PB = {x + 1} cm, then P is on the perpendicular bisector of [AB].
wrong.explain: P is on the perpendicular bisector only if PA = PB. Here {x} ≠ {x + 1}.
